meta.title: The Luhn algorithm explained
meta.description: How the Luhn algorithm works: right-to-left traversal, doubling every other digit, modulo-9 reduction, and modulo-10 test. With commented TypeScript code and the IIN prefix table.

algorithmPage.title: The Luhn algorithm, in detail
algorithmPage.description: Patented in 1960 by Hans Peter Luhn, an engineer at IBM, this calculation is used today in bank card numbers, phone IMEIs, and several national identifiers.

principle.title: What a checksum is for
principle.p1: A checksum adds redundancy to a sequence of digits to detect transmission or input errors. The last digit of a card number, called the {key}, is not chosen freely: it is calculated from all the preceding ones.
principle.p2After: of errors affecting a single digit, and nearly all transpositions of two adjacent digits — the two most common typing mistakes. Its known limitation: it cannot tell apart the transposition

items.step1: Write out the number and read it from right to left, starting with the check digit.
items.step2: Double every other digit, starting with the second-to-last one (the check digit is never doubled).
items.step3: If a doubling exceeds 9, subtract 9 from it — which amounts to adding its two digits together.
items.step4: Add up all the resulting values.
items.step5: If the sum is divisible by 10, the number is structurally consistent.

example.title: Example with 8 digits
example.intro: Let's take {number}. The top row gives the original digit, the bottom row its value after processing. The last {lastDigit} is the check digit: it is never doubled.
example.tableCaption: Breakdown of the Luhn calculation for the number 4539 1489
example.summary: Sum: 8 + 5 + 6 + 9 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 9 = {total}. Since {total} modulo 10 is 0, the structure is consistent. Change a single digit and the remainder stops being zero: that's the whole point of a checksum. The blue cells mark the doubled digits.

implementation.title: TypeScript implementation
implementation.description: A pure function, with no dependencies, in about fifteen lines. The site's full version also returns the detail of each step, for educational display.

prefixes.title: IIN prefixes and lengths by network
prefixes.description: Luhn says nothing about the issuing network. That is deduced from the first digits, the IIN ({term}), standardized by ISO/IEC 7812.

limits.title: What Luhn does not do
limits.alertBody: A number validated by Luhn is not a valid number. It is simply well-formed. The algorithm ignores the account's existence, its balance, its expiry date, and its status. Generating digit sequences that pass the test is trivial — which is exactly why payment networks rely on an online bank authorization, never on a checksum.
limits.conclusion: The legitimate use of client-side Luhn checking therefore comes down to one point: avoiding an unnecessary network round trip when the input clearly contains a typo.

meta.title: Privacy
meta.description: Card Verify collects no personal data: numbers entered are analyzed locally in the browser and are never transmitted, logged, or stored.

privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.intro: The principle is simple: what isn't collected can't leak.
privacyPage.verifyAlertBody: Open your browser's developer tools, “Network” tab, then enter a number on the demonstration page. No request appears.

noCollection.title: No number collection
noCollection.body: Numbers entered in the demonstration are processed exclusively by JavaScript code running in your browser. They are never transmitted to any server, never appear in any log, and are never written to cookies, local storage, or session storage.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: The site only sets a technical cookie to remember your language preference. No advertising tracker, no third-party audience-measurement tool is included.

logs.title: Technical logs
logs.body: The host may retain access logs (IP address, requested page, timestamp) for security and operational reasons. These logs never contain the form's content, since it never leaves the browser.

fonts.title: Fonts and external resources
fonts.body: The Inter font is loaded via next/font, which self-hosts it at build time. No request is therefore made to any third-party service during your visit.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: Since no personal data is collected by the site itself, there is no processing on which to exercise a right of access, rectification, or erasure. For any question, the contact page remains available to you.

notFoundPage.title: This page does not exist
